questions.question: Choose the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence. The war was followed by a long period of prosperity.
questions.questionHtml:
Choose the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence.
The war was followed by a long period of prosperity.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Failure.

Key Points

  • The word "prosperity" means a state of being successful, usually by making a lot of money. (समृद्धि )
    • Example: The country enjoyed a period of peace and prosperity after the war.
  • "Failure" refers to the lack of success or the inability to meet an expectation. (असफलता)
    • Example: The project ended in failure due to poor planning.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'prosperity' is 'failure'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Failure.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Security (सुरक्षा): The state of being free from danger or threat.
    • Example: The government has increased security at all airports.
  • Secure (सुरक्षित): Fixed or fastened so as not to give way, become loose, or be lost.
    • Example: Please make sure the doors are secure before you leave.
  • Affluence (धनाढ्यता): The state of having a great deal of money; wealth.
    • Example: His affluence is evident from the luxurious lifestyle he leads.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. Martha made pancakes yesterday.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Martha made pancakes yesterday.

options.text: Pancakes had been made by Martha yesterday.
options.html: Pancakes had been made by Martha yesterday.

options.text: Pancakes were being made by Martha yesterday.
options.html: Pancakes were being made by Martha yesterday.

options.text: Pancakes were made by Martha yesterday.
options.html: Pancakes were made by Martha yesterday.

options.text: Pancakes was made by Martha yesterday.
options.html: Pancakes was made by Martha yesterday.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the active voice, the sentence is: "Martha made pancakes yesterday."
  • To convert to passive voice: Place the object "pancakes" at the beginning.
  • Change the active verb form "made" to "were made" (past simple passive).
  • Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Martha."
  • Ensure the time phrase "yesterday" remains at the end of the sentence for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.
 
Correct Sentence: "Pancakes were made by Martha yesterday."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "Pancakes had been made by Martha yesterday." – Incorrect tense (past perfect passive).
  • Option 2: "Pancakes were being made by Martha yesterday." – Incorrect tense (past continuous passive).
  • Option 4: "Pancakes was made by Martha yesterday." – Subject-verb agreement error.

questions.question: In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement. O: also benefit from knowing P: there are several reasons Q: why even parents would R: more about how and why S: children do the things that they do
questions.questionHtml:
In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent
statement.
O: also benefit from knowing
P: there are several reasons
Q: why even parents would
R: more about how and why
S: children do the things that they do
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence construction begins by stating the existence of multiple reasons, establishing the context:
    • "There are several reasons why even parents would also benefit from knowing more about how and why children do the things that they do."
  • Sentence P is the first sentence as it introduces the existence of several reasons:
    • "There are several reasons"
  • Sentence Q follows as it begins to explain who benefits from these reasons:
    • "why even parents would"
  • Sentence O is the next part as it expands on the benefits that parents would have:
    • "also benefit from knowing"
  • Sentence R follows as it begins to detail what parents would know more about:
    • "more about how and why"
  • Sentence S is the concluding part as it completes the thought with the specific actions of children:
    • "children do the things that they do"
  • The correct sequence is PQORS.
 
Coherent sentence after rearrangement:
"There are several reasons why even parents would also benefit from knowing more about how and why children do the things that they do."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom. Radhika stood by Monica's side through thick and thin.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Radhika stood by Monica's side through thick and thin.

options.text: Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica's safety and security
options.html: Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica's safety and security

options.text: In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time
options.html: In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time

options.text: Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult
options.html: Under all conditions, no matter how challenging or difficult

options.text: In the moments when Monica couldn't complete some simple tasks
options.html: In the moments when Monica couldn't complete some simple tasks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 3.

Key Points

  • The idiom "through thick and thin" means supporting someone in all circumstances, good or bad, no matter how difficult. (अच्छे और बुरे समय में)
    • Example: True friends will stand by you through thick and thin, no matter what happens.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Option 1: Under easy situations wherein she could ensure Monica's safety and security (सिर्फ आसान परिस्थितियों में समर्थन देना): Supporting only in simple and safe conditions.
    • Example: She helps her friends only when things are going smoothly.
  • Option 2: In all the happy moments, personally spending most of her time (सिर्फ खुशहाल क्षणों में साथ रहना): Being with someone only during joyful times.
    • Example: She enjoys celebrating with friends in their happy times.
  • Option 4: In the moments when Monica couldn't complete some simple tasks (सिर्फ तब मदद करना जब वे सरल कार्यों में असफल हों): Helping someone only when they struggle with simple tasks.
    • Example: She only steps in to help when her friend faces minor difficulties.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence. His approach was filled with such perseverance that it was difficult to overlook his merit.

  • "Doggedness" refers to the quality of being determined to achieve something despite difficulties. (हठधर्मिता)

Additional Information

    • Example: His job became monotonous over the years, leading him to look for new opportunities.

questions.question: Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select 'No error' if there is no error. Although the team had trained diligently for months , they had still overwhelmed by the opponent's unexpected tactics.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the given sentence have been underlined. Identify the part that has an error. Select 'No error' if there is no error.
Although the team had trained diligently for months, they had still overwhelmed by the opponent's unexpected tactics.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The error lies in the phrase “had still overwhelmed”.
  • The verb form “overwhelmed” is incorrect here as it does not match the intended passive voice structure.
  • The correct form should be “had still been overwhelmed”, indicating that the team was affected by the opponent’s tactics.
  • In the past perfect tense, when expressing a passive action, the structure should be: had + been + past participle.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.
 
Correct Sentence: “Although the team had trained diligently for months, they had still been overwhelmed by the opponent's unexpected tactics.”

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word. If someone babbles , it means that they talk in a confused or excited way.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
If someone babbles, it means that they talk in a confused or excited way.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Quiet.

Key Points

  • The word "babble" means to talk in a confused or excited way. (बड़बड़ाना)
    • Example: The toddler started to babble as soon as she saw her favorite toy.
  • "Quiet" refers to making very little or no noise; it is the opposite of talking excessively or noisily. (शांत)
    • Example: The library is a quiet place where people can read and study without distractions.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'babble' is 'quiet'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Quiet.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Gossips (गपशप): Talking casually or informally about others, often involving details that are not confirmed as true.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank. Akash went to ______ his school uniform. [sell]
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in the brackets to fill in the blank.

  • The word "sell" means to give something in exchange for money. (बेचना)

  • "Buy" refers to acquiring something in exchange for money; it is the opposite action of selling. (खरीदना)
    • Example: He went to the market to buy fresh vegetables.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'sell' is 'buy'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. buy.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Loan (ऋण): A thing that is borrowed, especially a sum of money that is expected to be paid back with interest.

  • Rent (किराया): A tenant's regular payment to a landlord for the use of property or land.
    • Example: They decided to rent an apartment in the city.
  • Make (बनाना): Form (something) by putting parts together or combining substances; create.
    • Example: She loves to make handmade gifts for her friends.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence. Carnatic music is usually performed by a small troupe of actors , consisting of a principal performer, a melodic accompaniment, and a rhythm accompaniment.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined word segment in the given sentence.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence and forms a meaningful sentence. In November, Lakshman fell (P) / with fever (Q) / seriously ill (R) and pneumonia (S).
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that gives their correct logical sequence and forms a meaningful sentence.

In November, Lakshman fell (P) / with fever (Q) / seriously ill (R) and pneumonia (S).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 2 (P, R, Q, S).  

Lakshman first fell (P), then became seriously ill (R), followed by developing fever (Q) and pneumonia (S). The sequence logically captures the progression of events: falling ill, worsening condition, symptoms, and diagnosis.  

"Fell" (P) introduces the situation, "seriously ill" (R) intensifies it, "fever" (Q) describes a symptom, and "pneumonia" (S) identifies the illness, making this sequence accurate.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into five segments. The first segment has no error. Select the option that has the segment with the grammatical error. Due to the pandemic, / the prices of / medicines increased / every day since / last December.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into five segments. The first segment has no error. Select the option that has the segment with the grammatical error.
Due to the pandemic, / the prices of / medicines increased / every day since / last December.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the tense.
  • Since the sentence refers to a period starting in the past and continuing to the present, the present perfect tense should be used.
  • The correct phrase should be "medicines have increased," ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part C of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is C.
 
Correct Sentence: "Due to the pandemic, the prices of medicines have increased every day since last December."

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. I will be gifted a fancy doll by them the next day.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
I will be gifted a fancy doll by them the next day.

options.text: They gifted me a fancy doll yesterday.
options.html: They gifted me a fancy doll yesterday.

options.text: They are gifting me a fancy doll the next day.
options.html: They are gifting me a fancy doll the next day.

options.text: They gift me a fancy doll the previous day.
options.html: They gift me a fancy doll the previous day.

options.text: They will gift me a fancy doll tomorrow.
options.html: They will gift me a fancy doll tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4.
 
Key Points
  • Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
  • In the passive voice, the sentence is: "I will be gifted a fancy doll by them the next day."
  • To convert to active voice: Place the subject "they" at the beginning.
  • Change the passive verb form "will be gifted" to "will gift" (future simple active).
  • Ensure the time phrase "the next day" is appropriately changed to "tomorrow" for clarity.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.
 
Correct Sentence: "They will gift me a fancy doll tomorrow."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 1: "They gifted me a fancy doll yesterday." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to past simple.
  • Option 2: "They are gifting me a fancy doll the next day." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to present continuous.
  • Option 3: "They gift me a fancy doll the previous day." – Incorrect because it changes the tense and time reference.

Note: This is a PYP question, and the official answer key has marked (correct option) as the correct answer, hence we cannot make any changes to it.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence requires a word that shows the beginning of an event that happens after a short time or immediately.
  • 'When' is the most appropriate option as it introduces a specific time or condition when something happens.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.
 
Additional Information
  • 'Sooner' would not work because it suggests something should happen before another event, which doesn't match the passage's structure.
  • 'For' is used to indicate a reason or purpose and does not fit the requirement of introducing a specific event in time.
  • 'Unless' introduces a condition or exception and does not fit the intended meaning in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'having'.
 
Key Points
  • The sentence structure requires a participle form to describe Asha’s state while performing another action (flying to Switzerland).
  • Among the options, “having” correctly introduces a participial phrase — “having seen another grandchild safely into the world” — which expresses a completed action before the next event.
  • The other options (have, has, had) would make the sentence grammatically incorrect or awkward.
  • Thus, “having” fits best to indicate that Asha had already seen another grandchild before leaving for Switzerland.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
 
Complete Sentence: “Asha, having seen another grandchild safely into the world, was flying to Switzerland to be with her.”
 
Additional Information
  • Have – used with plural subjects or in present perfect tense; does not fit here.
  • Has – used with singular subjects in present perfect tense; incorrect due to tense mismatch.
  • Had – denotes past perfect but does not create the participial phrase needed in this context.
  • Having – forms a perfect participle phrase that correctly links two past actions.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'pursed'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage describes a character's reaction, where "pursed" refers to the action of tightening or pressing the lips together, often showing disapproval or displeasure.
  • "Pursed" fits the context as it suggests Nanda Kaul's reaction to the information, likely indicating a moment of distaste or frustration.
  • Other options like "stuck", "dirt", and "dusted" do not align with the context of describing a facial expression in this particular scenario.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
 
Additional Information
